**Puno** (Spanish pronunciation:[[ˈpuno]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"); [Aymara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aymara_language "Aymara language") and [Quechua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quechuan_languages "Quechuan languages"): _Punu_) is a [department of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regions_of_Peru "Regions of Peru"). Located in the country's southeast, it is the fifth largest department in Peru, after [Cuzco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Cuzco "Department of Cuzco"), [Madre de Dios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Madre_de_Dios "Department of Madre de Dios"), [Ucayali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Ucayali "Department of Ucayali"), and [Loreto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Loreto "Department of Loreto"). It is bordered by [Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia "Bolivia") to the east, the departments of [Madre de Dios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madre_de_Dios_Region "Madre de Dios Region") to the north, [Cusco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cusco_Region "Cusco Region") and [Arequipa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Arequipa "Department of Arequipa") to the west, [Moquegua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Moquegua "Department of Moquegua") to the southwest, and [Tacna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tacna_Region "Tacna Region") to the south. It is administered by a [regional government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_Government_of_Puno "Regional Government of Puno"). Its capital is the city of [Puno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puno "Puno"), which is located on [Lake Titicaca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Titicaca "Lake Titicaca") in the geographical region known as the [Altiplano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altiplano "Altiplano") or high sierra.

According to the adjusted 2025 census results, 1,233,000 people lived in Puno.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puno_Department#cite_note-1)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Department_of_Puno&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Puno was the territory of the [Tiahuanacos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiwanaku_empire "Tiwanaku empire") (800 A.D. – 1200 A.D.), who were the highest cultural expression of the Aymara people who established themselves in what is today Peru and Bolivia. The Incas took over these lands in the fifteenth century, and the Spanish, attracted by the mining industry developed there, left an important Colonial legacy throughout the entire area.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The department was created by the _Reglamento Provisional de Elecciones_, published on April 26, 1822, which established the department of Puno alongside those of [Arequipa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Arequipa "Department of Arequipa"), [Cuzco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Cusco "Department of Cusco"), [Huamanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Ayacucho "Department of Ayacucho"), and [Huancavelica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Huancavelica "Department of Huancavelica").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puno_Department#cite_note-2)

In department was the site of the [2007 Carancas impact event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Carancas_impact_event "2007 Carancas impact event").

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Department_of_Puno&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

The department of Puno is located in the [Collao Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altiplano "Altiplano"). The western part of [Lake Titicaca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Titicaca "Lake Titicaca"), which is the world's highest navigable lake, is located in the department. The [Andean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andes "Andes") mountains make up 70% of the region's territory, and the rest is covered by the [Amazon rainforest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_rainforest "Amazon rainforest").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puno_Department#cite_note-3)

The lake contains numerous islands whose inhabitants continue to live as their ancestors have in custom and tradition. The Uros an example of this; this people group lives on "floating islands" that they have artificially made entirely of totora reeds, and they navigate in their traditional boats also made out of totora reeds. Taquile, Suasi, and Amantaní are known for their kindness of their residents, their ancestral skill in weaving, their pre-Columbian constructions, and lovely countryside. The Titicaca National Reserve (36,180 hectares) protects extensive stretches of totora reeds and various species of plants and animals.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puno_Department#cite_note-4)

The climate is cold and dry, with a four-month rain season. On the other hand, the climate of the rainforest is warm. The water resources are taken from the Lake Titicaca, 50 lagoons and more than 300 rivers. There is also an important potential in underground waters.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Department_of_Puno&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 11: icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/60px-Question_book-new.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Question_book-new.svg)This section **does not [cite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources") any [sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")**. Please help [improve this section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:EditPage/Department_of_Puno "Special:EditPage/Department of Puno") by [adding citations to reliable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Referencing_for_beginners "Help:Referencing for beginners"). Unsourced material may be challenged and [removed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Burden_of_evidence "Wikipedia:Verifiability")._(January 2023)_ _([Learn how and when to remove this message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Maintenance\_template\_removal "Help:Maintenance template removal"))_

In ancient times, the Collao plateau was inhabited by [Aymara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aymara_people "Aymara people") groups (Collas or [Qolla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qulla_Kingdom "Qulla Kingdom"), Zapanas, Kallahuayos and [Lupacas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lupaca "Lupaca")). The [Quechuas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quechuas "Quechuas") came later.

According to chronicler [Inca Garcilaso de la Vega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inca_Garcilaso_de_la_Vega "Inca Garcilaso de la Vega"), these ancient times coincide with the legend of [Manco Cápac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manco_C%C3%A1pac "Manco Cápac") and [Mama Ocllo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama_Ocllo "Mama Ocllo"), who emerged from the waters of Lake Titicaca to found the [Inca Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inca_Empire "Inca Empire").

The [Aymara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aymara_people "Aymara people") culture, also known as Putina, was the most important and influential pre-[Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain") culture in the region.

During the Viceroyship, Puno was the obliged route for travelers going to Potosí, [Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia "Bolivia"). In 1668, viceroy [Conde de Lemos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conde_de_Lemos "Conde de Lemos") established San Juan Bautista de Puno as the capital of the province of Paucarcolla. Later, it was called San Carlos de Puno, in honor of the ruling king, [Charles II of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_II_of_Spain "Charles II of Spain"). The town was the capital of the [Intendancy of Puno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intendancy_of_Puno "Intendancy of Puno").

In 1870, the railway route [Arequipa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arequipa "Arequipa")-Puno was installed and navigation in Lake Titicaca started.

In 2007, a [meteorite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carancas_impact_event "Carancas impact event") landed in the region, triggering a widespread illness amongst the locals. The exact cause of the illness is unknown, but is speculated to be a result of arsenic or other toxic chemicals that may have been released by the heat of impact.

## Language and ethnicity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Department_of_Puno&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Language and ethnicity")]

Indigenous people are the majority in the Puno region. As of 2011[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Department_of_Puno&action=edit), 41.4% of Puno's inhabitants speak [Quechua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quechua_languages "Quechua languages"), 30.39% speak [Aymara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aymara_language "Aymara language"); 0.05% speak Ashaninka; and 0.03% speak another indigenous language. Monolingual Spanish speakers make up 28.1% of the population.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puno_Department#cite_note-5)

According to the [2007 Peru Census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Peru_Census "2007 Peru Census"), the language learnt first by most of the residents was [Quechua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quechua_language "Quechua language") (38.01%) followed by [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language") (34.81%) and [Aymara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aymara_language "Aymara language") (26.93%). The Quechua variety spoken in Puno is [Cusco–Collao Quechua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cusco%E2%80%93Collao_Quechua "Cusco–Collao Quechua"). **Puno** (Spanish pronunciation:[[ˈpuno]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"); [Aymara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aymara_language "Aymara language") and [Quechua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quechuan_languages "Quechuan languages"): _Punu_) is a [department of Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regions_of_Peru "Regions of Peru"). Located in the country's southeast, it is the fifth largest department in Peru, after [Cuzco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Cuzco "Department of Cuzco"), [Madre de Dios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Madre_de_Dios "Department of Madre de Dios"), [Ucayali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Ucayali "Department of Ucayali"), and [Loreto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Loreto "Department of Loreto"). It is bordered by [Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia "Bolivia") to the east, the departments of [Madre de Dios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madre_de_Dios_Region "Madre de Dios Region") to the north, [Cusco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cusco_Region "Cusco Region") and [Arequipa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Arequipa "Department of Arequipa") to the west, [Moquegua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Moquegua "Department of Moquegua") to the southwest, and [Tacna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tacna_Region "Tacna Region") to the south. It is administered by a [regional government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_Government_of_Puno "Regional Government of Puno"). Its capital is the city of [Puno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puno "Puno"), which is located on [Lake Titicaca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Titicaca "Lake Titicaca") in the geographical region known as the [Altiplano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altiplano "Altiplano") or high sierra.

According to the adjusted 2025 census results, 1,233,000 people lived in Puno.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puno_Department#cite_note-1)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Department_of_Puno&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Puno was the territory of the [Tiahuanacos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiwanaku_empire "Tiwanaku empire") (800 A.D. – 1200 A.D.), who were the highest cultural expression of the Aymara people who established themselves in what is today Peru and Bolivia. The Incas took over these lands in the fifteenth century, and the Spanish, attracted by the mining industry developed there, left an important Colonial legacy throughout the entire area.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The department was created by the _Reglamento Provisional de Elecciones_, published on April 26, 1822, which established the department of Puno alongside those of [Arequipa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Arequipa "Department of Arequipa"), [Cuzco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Cusco "Department of Cusco"), [Huamanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Ayacucho "Department of Ayacucho"), and [Huancavelica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Huancavelica "Department of Huancavelica").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puno_Department#cite_note-2)

In department was the site of the [2007 Carancas impact event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Carancas_impact_event "2007 Carancas impact event").

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Department_of_Puno&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

The department of Puno is located in the [Collao Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altiplano "Altiplano"). The western part of [Lake Titicaca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Titicaca "Lake Titicaca"), which is the world's highest navigable lake, is located in the department. The [Andean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andes "Andes") mountains make up 70% of the region's territory, and the rest is covered by the [Amazon rainforest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_rainforest "Amazon rainforest").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puno_Department#cite_note-3)

The lake contains numerous islands whose inhabitants continue to live as their ancestors have in custom and tradition. The Uros an example of this; this people group lives on "floating islands" that they have artificially made entirely of totora reeds, and they navigate in their traditional boats also made out of totora reeds. Taquile, Suasi, and Amantaní are known for their kindness of their residents, their ancestral skill in weaving, their pre-Columbian constructions, and lovely countryside. The Titicaca National Reserve (36,180 hectares) protects extensive stretches of totora reeds and various species of plants and animals.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puno_Department#cite_note-4)

The climate is cold and dry, with a four-month rain season. On the other hand, the climate of the rainforest is warm. The water resources are taken from the Lake Titicaca, 50 lagoons and more than 300 rivers. There is also an important potential in underground waters.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Department_of_Puno&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 11: icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/60px-Question_book-new.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Question_book-new.svg)This section **does not [cite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources") any [sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")**. Please help [improve this section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:EditPage/Department_of_Puno "Special:EditPage/Department of Puno") by [adding citations to reliable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Referencing_for_beginners "Help:Referencing for beginners"). Unsourced material may be challenged and [removed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Burden_of_evidence "Wikipedia:Verifiability")._(January 2023)_ _([Learn how and when to remove this message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Maintenance\_template\_removal "Help:Maintenance template removal"))_

In ancient times, the Collao plateau was inhabited by [Aymara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aymara_people "Aymara people") groups (Collas or [Qolla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qulla_Kingdom "Qulla Kingdom"), Zapanas, Kallahuayos and [Lupacas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lupaca "Lupaca")). The [Quechuas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quechuas "Quechuas") came later.

According to chronicler [Inca Garcilaso de la Vega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inca_Garcilaso_de_la_Vega "Inca Garcilaso de la Vega"), these ancient times coincide with the legend of [Manco Cápac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manco_C%C3%A1pac "Manco Cápac") and [Mama Ocllo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama_Ocllo "Mama Ocllo"), who emerged from the waters of Lake Titicaca to found the [Inca Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inca_Empire "Inca Empire").

The [Aymara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aymara_people "Aymara people") culture, also known as Putina, was the most important and influential pre-[Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain") culture in the region.

During the Viceroyship, Puno was the obliged route for travelers going to Potosí, [Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia "Bolivia"). In 1668, viceroy [Conde de Lemos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conde_de_Lemos "Conde de Lemos") established San Juan Bautista de Puno as the capital of the province of Paucarcolla. Later, it was called San Carlos de Puno, in honor of the ruling king, [Charles II of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_II_of_Spain "Charles II of Spain"). The town was the capital of the [Intendancy of Puno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intendancy_of_Puno "Intendancy of Puno").

In 1870, the railway route [Arequipa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arequipa "Arequipa")-Puno was installed and navigation in Lake Titicaca started.

In 2007, a [meteorite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carancas_impact_event "Carancas impact event") landed in the region, triggering a widespread illness amongst the locals. The exact cause of the illness is unknown, but is speculated to be a result of arsenic or other toxic chemicals that may have been released by the heat of impact.

## Language and ethnicity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Department_of_Puno&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Language and ethnicity")]

Indigenous people are the majority in the Puno region. As of 2011[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Department_of_Puno&action=edit), 41.4% of Puno's inhabitants speak [Quechua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quechua_languages "Quechua languages"), 30.39% speak [Aymara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aymara_language "Aymara language"); 0.05% speak Ashaninka; and 0.03% speak another indigenous language. Monolingual Spanish speakers make up 28.1% of the population.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puno_Department#cite_note-5)

According to the [2007 Peru Census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Peru_Census "2007 Peru Census"), the language learnt first by most of the residents was [Quechua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quechua_language "Quechua language") (38.01%) followed by [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language") (34.81%) and [Aymara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aymara_language "Aymara language") (26.93%). The Quechua variety spoken in Puno is [Cusco–Collao Quechua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cusco%E2%80%93Collao_Quechua "Cusco–Collao Quechua").
